newsitem.title: USA: Tobacco plaintiff can seek punitive damages.
newsitem.headline: Tobacco plaintiff can seek punitive damages.

text.p: A Florida judge has ruled that a plaintiff in a wrongful death case against a tobacco company can ask a jury to award punitive damages.

In the ruling, filed with the clerk's office Monday, Circuit Judge Bernard Nachman said evidence presented by lawyers for plaintiff Dana Raulerson was sufficient to indicate that R.J. Reynolds knew cigarettes were dangerous.

Raulerson sued the tobacco company as a representative of the estate of her sister, Jean Connor, a smoker who filed a product liability suit against Reynolds in March 1995 but died of lung cancer that fall.

Attorney Norwood Wilner, Raulerson's lawyer, has said this would be the first time a single plaintiff in a Florida tobacco case has been allowed to argue for punitive damages against a tobacco company. Trial was scheduled for April 7.

In a Jan. 23 hearing, Wilner cited thousands of documents that he said showed cigarettes are a dangerous and defective product. An attorney for Reynolds, a unit of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp., countered that the case did not meet the state's standard for punitive damages.

Last August, one of Wilner's clients, Grady Carter of Orange Park, Fla., and his wife, won a $750,000 jury award in his product liability lawsuit against B.A.T Industries Plc's Brown & Williamson Tobacco Corp.
